why: Unauthorised geofence modification can permit restricted-airspace entry, creating serious safety and regulatory consequences.
Centralised telemetry poisoning can simultaneously corrupt mandatory services and undermine safety-critical operational decisions.
Unverified meteorological and traffic feeds can generate unsafe routing decisions and propagate misleading operational information.
Log destruction compromises incident reconstruction, accountability and mandatory regulatory evidence retention.
Credential compromise enables scalable operational-data exfiltration, affecting confidentiality and dependent services.
Database compromise enables extensive operational-data corruption, exfiltration and disruption of dependent U-Space services.
Compromised oversight records undermine enforcement, accountability and compliance assurance across the U-Space ecosystem.
Regulatory ambiguity can systematically weaken cybersecurity governance and compliance across every architectural layer.
Strategic information disclosure provides adversarial intelligence but has no direct operational safety consequence.
GNSS spoofing and jamming can directly compromise aircraft navigation, causing restricted-airspace incursions or loss of control.
C2 disruption during BVLOS operations can cause uncontrolled aircraft behaviour, collisions and loss of aircraft.
Persistent flight-controller compromise can manipulate aircraft behaviour and cause crashes, with difficult firmware remediation.
Power and battery-management compromise can interrupt operations or cause uncontrolled landings and aircraft loss.
Manipulated altitude, position or inertial measurements can directly corrupt flight decisions and cause collisions.
Physical sabotage of vertiport controls can compromise landing operations and create direct risks to people and aircraft.
Trusted supply-chain compromise can distribute persistent malicious firmware across fleets and multiple architectural layers.
Identity spoofing enables unauthorised and unaccountable operations, undermining identification and regulatory compliance.
False aircraft positions can conceal genuine conflicts and defeat safety-critical traffic monitoring and separation functions.
Authorisation bypass can permit illegal flights and restricted-airspace access, directly undermining critical flight-safety barriers.
Publicly reachable gateway flooding can disable mandatory services fleet-wide, interrupting flight authorisation and service continuity.
Falsified geofence information can authorise unsafe routing into restricted airspace and propagate across dependent services.
